uniqueness.difference: signals come from the resting book, the quote against the liquidation mark and the book before the daily funding print: fields no candle carries
uniqueness.family_flag: none (book and liquidation structure); a survivor is checked for correlation with perps momentum before it is called unique

data.source: perp-live-data branch (record-perps-live.yml): markets.csv (bid, ask, sizes, last, marks, open interest, leverage estimates by size), book.csv (five levels nearest the touch, ONLY from the first file written after the book-level fix), static.csv, coverage.csv
data.ticker_names_note: names as seen in static.csv of the first file; the wall and its sha256 go into the spec before any outcome-bearing column is joined
data.independence_note: forward recorder data only; no earlier book exists

split.start_rule: provisional: 00:00 UTC of the first full UTC day after the FIRST recorder file written after the book fix is merged (Auditor B, 2026-11-16 20:46Z). The loader drops every earlier perp-live-data file whose book.csv holds far levels (cut keyed by the file's directory stamp, which Main records in this spec on merge) and COUNTS the dropped files. If that first fixed file is not written before 2026-11-17T20:00Z the start_utc constant moves to the next midnight by a dated amendment BEFORE any outcome column is joined; no amendment after. Rows of dropped files may feed only the trailing medians of F2 (quote spread, which the fix does not touch), never F1 or F4.
split.warmup: rows of a ticker before start_utc feed only the trailing medians; no trade is entered before start_utc
split.release_rule: one read per rule: at the first read date if the rule has 100 entries, else it is 'no evidence at n = x' there and is read once more on 2026-12-21 on the same constants; a rule that reached n >= 100 at the first read is never re-read

holds.label: H16 perps (KXSPYPERP*, KXQQQPERP*, KXNVDAPERP*, KXAAPLPERP*, KXUS500PERP*, KXUSTECH100PERP*)
holds.handling: last decision 1797811200 (2026-12-21T00:00Z); the longest hold (60 min) ends 01:00Z Dec 21 before 1797897600; applies to NVDA, US Tech 100 and US Large Cap. MU and TSLA are not in H16 (Auditor B confirmed MU; TSLA absent from his list)

F1_imbalance.def: I = (sum bid_sz_1..5 minus sum ask_sz_1..5) / (sum bid_sz_1..5 plus sum ask_sz_1..5) from book.csv at the decision minute
F1_imbalance.direction: follow: long when I >= T, short when I <= -T; fade: the reverse

F2_spread_widening.def: R = quoted spread in bps / the median of the same name's quoted spread over its previous 24 h of rows (at least 720 rows, else skipped and counted)
F2_spread_widening.direction: widening has no sign: direction is the sign of the mid change over the previous 5 minutes (follow = same way, fade = against); a flat 5 minute mid skips the decision

F3_liq_distance.def: D = (mid minus liquidation_mark_price) / mid in bps, mid = (bid + ask)/2 of the same minute's markets row
F3_liq_distance.direction: mid above the mark: fade = short, follow = long; mid below the mark: the reverse; |D| >= T

F4_pre_print_thinning.def: K = sum of the five levels' sizes on both sides / the median of the same name's total depth over the previous 24 h; decision minutes from 90 to 30 minutes before the daily 4 PM ET funding print only (21:00 UTC while New York is on standard time, which holds for the whole window); signal when K <= T
F4_pre_print_thinning.direction: sign of the book imbalance I at the decision minute (follow / fade); I = 0 skips
F4_pre_print_thinning.note: hold ends before the print (decision at most 30 minutes before the print and hold at most 30, so the exit is at or before the print minute); gold (14:00Z print) and crypto (print times unverified) are left out of F4

features.thresholds_note: all constants written now. F3 and F2 thresholds were chosen from signal COUNTS in the first 101 minute file (no outcome, no return was computed); F1 and F4 thresholds are round values with no data behind them (book unusable in that file).

episodes: a signal is the first minute a condition holds after it was false for at least 15 minutes; one position per name and rule at a time (no new entry until the hold ends); entry at the first recorded quote AFTER the decision minute (buy at the ask, sell at the bid), exit at the first quote at or after entry + hold (opposite touch); a missing quote within 2 minutes of the exit time voids the trade and counts it; an event whose hold spans a funding print is dropped and counted

grid.subset_rationale: the whole stated grid, fixed before any outcome exists

look_ahead.decision: markets and book rows with t_recv_ms at or before the end of the decision minute; trailing medians use only rows before it
look_ahead.entry: the first quote after the decision minute, never the decision row
look_ahead.exit: first quote at or after the hold; path test uses every recorded mid from entry to exit
look_ahead.funding: events whose hold spans a funding print are dropped and counted; funding is not in the recorder

costs.price_terms: net per trade in bps of entry notional: (exit touch minus entry touch)/entry touch x 1e4 for a long (negated for a short), the spread is paid by crossing the touch both ways, minus the fee
costs.fee_note: 12 and 5 bps are the Head's scenarios of 2026-11-16; Kalshi's published perps fee is still to be written in before the read and the two scenarios stay beside it. Every figure is labelled 'fee assumed, not a result' until then
costs.margin_terms: for each size key 1000 and 10000 (notional in dollars), L_max = the recorder's long_lev or short_lev estimate of that key at entry; leverage used = f x L_max with f = 10%, 25%, 50%; return on margin = net bps x leverage used; reported beside, never instead of, price terms
costs.liquidation_test: path based: with d_liq = (1/f - 1) / L_max (assumes maintenance margin equals the margin at maximum leverage, conservative, to be checked against Kalshi's margin rules), a trade whose worst recorded mid moves against it by d_liq or more before exit counts as liquidated and loses the whole margin (-1/(f L_max) x 1e4 bps of notional); the count of such trades is printed per f
costs.income: entries a day x mean net bps (price terms) x leverage used, ranked; figures by message only

gates.pf_note: PF 1.3 at fee 5 bps and PF 1.0 at fee 12 bps (the harsher cost), as the binary families use a lenient line and a harsh line
gates.signals_per_day_note: entries per active day of the name (weekdays; equities only inside their open session), over the days from start_utc to the read
gates.p: one sided, day clustered (UTC date of entry) on the 5 bps net

tries.prior_m: 6,290,660 (Head ruling 2026-11-16 18:35Z) for a print today; 7,492,484 carried from 2026-11-17 on (batch C registered 2026-11-16, Auditor B confirms Nov 17); m_total = carried + 906, with the 240 F1t cells counted once here

read_date.basis: only 101 minutes of data exist, so signal rates are a thin guide. Episodes seen in that file (15 minute lockout, before the position lockout): liquidation distance >= 1.0 to 3.0 bps about 0 to 4 per name per 101 minutes; spread >= 2x of the in-file median 0 to 3 per name per 101 minutes; zero at 5x and at 6 bps, which is why those thresholds are not used. At about 1 to 3 episodes per name per open hour a rule reaches 100 entries in roughly 5 to 20 open days (hold lockout lowers it); the 10 trade day floor then binds first for the faster rules, so 2026-12-08 is the first read, and slower rules (F4 has at most 20 decision minutes a day, F1 at 0.7) are expected to read 'no evidence at n = x' there and get the single read on 2026-12-21. The rate is re-measured from the first 3 full days and written as a dated note BEFORE any outcome column is joined; the dates do not move after that.

prediction: low prior: most rules fail the PF 1.3 / 1.0 pair at the 12 bps scenario because a 5 to 60 minute hold in a liquid perp earns well under 12 bps; expect at most a handful at 5 bps and none after BH
kill: drop the family if the first read has PF under 1.0 at fee 5 bps in at least 6 of the 8 markets for each feature
fee_form: perps: bps of notional, assumed; binary per-order rounding is not used

F1t_touch_imbalance.def: I1 = (bid_sz_1 - ask_sz_1) / (bid_sz_1 + ask_sz_1) from the book row at the decision poll; two sided top required (0 < bid_px_1 < ask_px_1, both sizes > 0), else skipped and counted
F1t_touch_imbalance.direction: follow or fade (follow = long when I1 >= T, short when I1 <= -T)
arms: F: book_fast.csv, the 5 second book, 14:30 to 21:00 UTC Monday to Friday, five fast tickers
S: book.csv, the 60 second book, all hours
